html:
The Chishti order is a Sufi brotherhood of Islam that took root in India when Moinuddin Chishti settled at Ajmer in Rajasthan around the time the Ghurids took north India in 1192.

The order is named after Chisht, a town in Afghanistan. Its Indian masters taught love of God, service to the poor and distance from kings. Their lodges ran open kitchens for anyone, Muslim or Hindu, and they used music and song in worship, the root of qawwali.

The line passed from teacher to student:

  • Moinuddin Chishti at Ajmer, died 1236.
  • Qutbuddin Bakhtiar Kaki in Delhi.
  • Baba Farid in Punjab, whose verses later went into the Sikh scripture.
  • Nizamuddin Auliya in Delhi, teacher of Amir Khusrau.

The Chishtis did much to spread Islam among ordinary people. Moinuddin's tomb at Ajmer became one of the great shrines of South Asia. Akbar walked there on foot to pray for a son, and millions still visit, of many faiths.
